traits.note: FNA vol. 28, Hylocomium (Rohrer; efloras, read 2026-11-06): stems creeping to more often arching-ascending, regularly 2- or 3-pinnate; capsule inclined to pendent; operculum conic, obliquely long-rostrate; one species. H. splendens (same volume, p. 328): plants to 20 cm; innovations forming ascending series of flat frondose tiers, fronds 20-35(-50) mm wide; primary branch leaves 0.8-1.3(-2) x 0.3-0.6(-0.9) mm; seta 0.5-2.5 cm; capsule mostly bent horizontal at the neck, ovoid to ellipsoid, 1.7-2.8 mm; on soil, humus, rotten logs and rock over extensive areas of forest, especially boreal conifer forests, also common in arctic and alpine tundra. PNW rainforest plants are robust, 3-pinnate, and form deep wefts of stair-step innovations.

traits.height_typical_m.note: The depth of a weft of stair-step fronds on shoots to 20 cm (FNA): deep in PNW forests, a few centimetres in the tundra form. Estimate.

traits.light.note: FNA vol. 28, Hylocomium splendens (efloras, read 2026-11-06): forest floors, and also arctic and alpine tundra, so shade to open.

traits.moisture.note: Moist forest floors and tundra; not on dry exposed ground. Estimate from the FNA habitats.

traits.capsule_share.note: Goffinet and Shaw, Bryophyte Biology (2009), p. 424 (as extracted 2026-10-15): dioicous; capsules rare, found only on the oldest uplift island studied. Share an estimate.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: One new frond a year, each arising from the back of the one before (Bryophyte Biology, p. 424, fig. 10.3), so a weft advances a few centimetres a year at most. Estimate.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Not measured yet: yellowish to olive green over red stems (Wikipedia, read 2026-11-06), so r/g 0.95, b/g 0.22, between Homalothecium and Hypnum; the brightness is a green reflectance of 0.13, as the other moss genera's colours take it (a lit leaf's, just above the 0.05-0.11 moss canopies reflect in the visible; see Hypnum's note). To measure with imagekit like the other genera.

traits.leaf_dry_posture.note: FNA vol. 28, Hylocomium (efloras, read 2026-11-06): stem leaves tightly appressed on the stipe to erect among the branches; primary branch leaves erect-spreading, concave. FNA gives no dry posture; the leaves change little on drying, so appressed.
